Present. MAJORITY LEADER FARÍAS: Thank you. We will now have today’s invocation, which will be delivered by Pastor Michael Walrond, Junior, Senior Pastor at First Corinthian Baptist Church, located at 1912 Adam Clayton Powell Boulevard in Manhattan. PASTOR MICHAEL WALROND,

[FEEDBACK] [INAUDIBLE]... Let us pray. God, we begin this time together by saying thank you, O God. Thank you for this day. Thank you for this time. Most of all, O God, we thank you, because on this day we remember that your grace is still sufficient; your mercy still endures, and your love still covers us. So, God, be with us. Be with us, O God, in a special way for these times, O God, are tumultuous. For we are in the moment, O God, where seemingly there is more hate than there is love, more violence than there is peace, and, O God, even more fiction than there is fact. So, God, be with us. Be with this body, O God, as they do the work of this city of behalf of the people of this city. And,

NEW YORK CITY COUNCIL STATED MEETING 10 O God, remind them that we need leaders in times like this; leaders, O God, who do not put political expediency before the needs of the people; leaders, O God, who are not so consumed with their own ego that they forget to honor your people in this city. We need leaders, O God, who are willing to stand for justice and righteousness and to honor, O God, even the least of these among us. So, God, be with these leaders; be with these servants as they move forward in this space, in this place, in this season, and in this time. And more than that, O God, remind them in these times filled with chaos and, at times, discord that we need love warriors, love revolutionaries, O God, who honor the inherent dignity of all of your children, who do not, O God, put their needs above the needs of your people, but who take love seriously, who lead with love, in love, through love, and for love. So, God, be with this body, and be with this city, O God, as we seek in our own way to intentionally be human. Most of all, O God, remind everyone gathered here today, that life begins to end the day we remain silent about things that matter. We love you, God, and it’s your name we pray. Amen.
